title: Finite reduction of the completed map
statement:
Use the adic datum, proper Cartesian square, derived complete $K$, and specified finite-level etale-origin witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map]. Use the named edges of [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square], and let $n\geq1$. For the final Frobenius assertion use the coherent Frobenius tower datum and the directly defined quotient-coefficient Weil structures of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures]. All four finite vertices and their Weil structures are in $D(Y'_{\mathrm{proet}},P_n)$; the completed vertices and their structures are over $A_{Y'}$.

For every $n$, the diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
S\otimes^LP_n @>{\overline\xi_n}>> T\otimes^LP_n\\
@V{\alpha_n}V{\sim}V @VV{\delta_n}V{\sim}\\
B_n @>{v'_n}>> D_n
\end{CD}
$$

commutes. Hence reduction of
$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] modulo $I^n$, conjugated
by the displayed canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly the S8
transported finite-level exchange map $v'_n=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}$.
The squares for $n+1\to n$ commute, and the assertion is natural for
compatible tower endomorphisms. Under a Frobenius-equivariant datum, use
$\Phi_{Y'}P_n=P_n$ to give the two reductions their induced Weil structures.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\alpha_n),\\
\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\delta_n),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the displayed reduction square is a square of Weil objects.

note:
*Source note:* the reduction of the completed pullback is the formula
$Lf^*_{comp}M=\Rlim Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n})$ of
Stacks Project, Lemma 61.20.2 ([Tag
099N](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/099N)), whose $n$-th level is
$Lf_n^*$ of the $n$-th level; Stacks states the formula for the completed
pullback of one object of $D(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$, whereas the displayed
statement reduces the completed base-change exchange map of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], which the verified entries
do not construct, and the blueprint adds that reduction together with its
compatibility with the transitions and with compatible endomorphisms.

proof.text:
First justify reduction for a possibly incomplete input. For $Z\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(Y'_{\Proet},A_{Y'}))$, set $Z_n=Z\otimes^L_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}$ and $\widehat Z=\Rlim Z_\bullet$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] on the small site $Y'_{\Proet}$. Its canonical finite-reduction comparison identifies the strict reduction towers of $\operatorname{Res}(Z)$ and $Z$, and its derived-limit comparison respects the completion units and evaluations. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] to $\operatorname{Res}(Z)$ with constant ring $\Lambda=A$. The hypotheses in [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] hold by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $A$ is Noetherian, $I$ is finitely generated, $A/I$ is additive torsion, and all $P_n$ are perfect. Transport its functorial, projection-adjoint isomorphism through the coefficient comparisons to obtain
$$q_{Z,n}:\widehat Z\otimes^L_{A_{Y'}}(P_n)_{Y'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_n.$$
It is the adjoint of evaluation to $Z_n$, natural in $Z$. This uses no completeness hypothesis on $Z$; in particular it does not apply the complete-input reconstruction theorem to an incomplete object.

source.place: Paragraph 1, functorial finite reduction; supplies the arbitrary-input reduction needed by the right edge

proof.text:
Use $S,T,\xi=\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map], and denote its first identification before $H$ by $s_A:S\xrightarrow{\sim}A_\infty$ and its direct-image comparison by $d:T\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\infty$. Thus $d\xi=V'Hs_A$. Put $N=Lg^*Rf_*K$ and $M=Rf'_*Lg'^*K$. Under [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] and the pullback/tensor comparisons specified in [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows], $A_\bullet,C_\bullet$ are their strict reduction towers. Write $q_{A,n}=q_{N,n}$ and $q_{C,n}=q_{M,n}$. Let $c:C_\infty\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ be the ordered map $\chi$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square]. Both the prescribed completed-pullback reduction and $q_{A,n}(s_A\otimes1)$ are adjoints of the same evaluation map; hence they coincide. The named edges are therefore
$$\sigma_n=q_{A,n}(s_A\otimes1),\quad \tau_n=q_{C,n}(c^{-1}\otimes1),\quad \alpha_n=h_n\sigma_n,\quad\delta_n=h'_n\tau_n.$$
Step 1 justifies the prescribed projection-induced reduction on $M$, even if $M$ is not complete. The use of completed-pullback reduction on $Rf_*K$ is legitimate: [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] says that this input is derived complete, as required by [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction].

source.place: Paragraph 1, the identifications S=A_infinity and T=C_infinity, and the named reduction edges

proof.text:
The ordered composite for $c$ in [def-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-square] is $\lambda_E^{-1}\Rlim(\pi_{f',E,P_m})$, for $E=Lg'^*K$. The canonical comparison $E\otimes^LP_m\simeq Lg_m'^*K_m$ in [def-weil-pbc-four-corners] identifies these projection-formula arrows with $h'_m$ of [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows]. They form the tower map of [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility]. The comparison $\lambda_E$ is $d$: both are the specified direct-image/derived-limit comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] on that same tower. Consequently $c=d^{-1}H'$, and $dc=H'$. The limit rectangle of [lem-weil-pbc-rectangle-derived-limit] gives $V'H=H'V$. Substituting in $d\xi=V'Hs_A$ and cancelling $d$ proves
$$\xi=cVs_A.$$
The comparison $dc=H'$ is an equality of the specified ordered composites, so no choice of a triangle filler enters it.

source.place: Paragraph 1, dc=H-prime and the limit rectangle

proof.text:
Let $e:N\to M$ be the ambient exchange. By [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows], $v_n$ is its reduction, with the prescribed pullback/tensor comparison; [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility] supplies the associated tower map, whose derived limit is $V$ by [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Apply the functorial reduction of [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] to $\operatorname{Res}(e)$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] to identify the towers and reductions. It gives
$$q_{C,n}(V\otimes1)=v_nq_{A,n}.$$
Tensoring step 3 and using step 2 now gives
$$\tau_n\overline\xi_n=q_{C,n}(c^{-1}\otimes1)(c\otimes1)(V\otimes1)(s_A\otimes1)=v_n\sigma_n.$$
The equality $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$ is exactly [lem-weil-pbc-finite-level-rectangle]. Therefore
$$\delta_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n=v'_n\alpha_n.$$
All four named reduction and projection-formula identifications are isomorphisms by steps 1--2 and [def-weil-pbc-four-arrows]. Thus $\delta_n\overline\xi_n\alpha_n^{-1}=v'_n$, the specified finite exchange, not an unspecified isomorphism.

For $Z=N,M$, let $\eta_Z:Z\to\widehat Z$ be its quotient-tower completion unit and $r^Z_{n+1,n}=1_Z\otimes(P_{n+1}\to P_n)$. Its projection to $Z_n$ is the scalar-extension unit. Since $q_{Z,n}$ is the adjoint of that projection, naturality and the triangle identity of extension/restriction adjunction give $q_{Z,n}(\eta_Z\otimes1)=1_{Z_n}$. Step 1 then gives $\eta_Z\otimes1=q_{Z,n}^{-1}$. These are the same units under [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], and the projection-adjoint property is [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction]. Tensor naturality for the fixed morphism $\eta_Z$ says
$$r^{\widehat Z}_{n+1,n}(\eta_Z\otimes1_{P_{n+1}})=(\eta_Z\otimes1_{P_n})r^Z_{n+1,n}.$$
Multiplying by the two inverses proves $r^Z_{n+1,n}q_{Z,n+1}=q_{Z,n}r^{\widehat Z}_{n+1,n}$. Composing with $s_A\otimes1$ and $c^{-1}\otimes1$ and using tensor naturality for these fixed maps gives
$$a_{n+1,n}\sigma_{n+1}=\sigma_nr^S_{n+1,n},\quad c_{n+1,n}\tau_{n+1}=\tau_nr^T_{n+1,n}.$$
Here every transition is in the ambient $A$-coefficient category; none is normalized tensor over $P_{n+1}$.

source.place: Paragraph 3, naturality of the reduction edges for consecutive quotient maps

proof.text:
The tower-map equations in [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility] are
$$b_{n+1,n}h_{n+1}=h_na_{n+1,n},\quad d_{n+1,n}h'_{n+1}=h'_nc_{n+1,n},\quad d_{n+1,n}v'_{n+1}=v'_nb_{n+1,n}.$$
Substituting step 5 into the first two gives
$$b_{n+1,n}\alpha_{n+1}=\alpha_nr^S_{n+1,n},\qquad d_{n+1,n}\delta_{n+1}=\delta_nr^T_{n+1,n}.$$
Finally, since $\overline\xi_n=\xi\otimes1_{P_n}$, tensor naturality gives $r^T_{n+1,n}\overline\xi_{n+1}=\overline\xi_nr^S_{n+1,n}$. These identities and the displayed equation for $v'$ give every edge of the transition between the two reduction squares.

For a compatible tower endomorphism of $K_\bullet$, first define $u_K=\eta_K^{-1}\Rlim(u_\bullet)\eta_K$ using the completeness identification $\eta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Rlim K_\bullet$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map]. Naturality of the evaluation maps in [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle], followed by their scalar-extension adjuncts, identifies its reduction with the given $u_n$. Thus it suffices to use an endomorphism of $K$. For a compatible endomorphism of $K$, write $u_{Z,n}$ and $u_{Z,\infty}$ for its induced maps on each corner tower and limit, and $u_S,u_T$ for the completed objects. By [lem-weil-pbc-tower-compatibility], all four finite edges intertwine these maps. Applying the functor [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] gives the same identities for $H,V,H',V'$. Functoriality of completed-pullback reduction [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction] and of the canonical comparison [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] gives
$$s_Au_S=u_{A,\infty}s_A,\qquad du_T=u_{D,\infty}d.$$
Since $c=d^{-1}H'$, these imply $cu_{C,\infty}=u_Tc$. Step 1's functoriality, namely [lemma-weil-pbc-adic-completion-reduction] through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], gives
$$q_{A,n}(u_{A,\infty}\otimes1)=u_{A,n}q_{A,n},\quad q_{C,n}(u_{C,\infty}\otimes1)=u_{C,n}q_{C,n}.$$
Substitution in step 2 proves $\alpha_n(u_S\otimes1)=u_{B,n}\alpha_n$ and $\delta_n(u_T\otimes1)=u_{D,n}\delta_n$. Step 3 gives $\xi u_S=cVu_{A,\infty}s_A=cu_{C,\infty}Vs_A=u_T\xi$; tensoring gives the upper-edge identity. The lower-edge identity is $v'_nu_{B,n}=u_{D,n}v'_n$. This proves the endomorphism clause on every edge.

Use [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures] from now on. Its coefficient maps for $F_T$ and all square edges commute with $A_T\to(P_n)_T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Thus every Frobenius face is a square of ringed topoi at both coefficient levels. Its $\beta$ is an isomorphism: paste that face with the face for the inverse automorphisms. By the two pasting identities and identity case of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], the composites of their exchange maps, with the inverse-image composition identifications inserted, are identity transformations. These are two-sided inverses. The same argument works on the ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. The $\kappa$ maps are the specified invertible pullback-composition comparisons. Hence the displayed composites defining $\Theta_B,\Theta_D$, and their finite/ambient strict transports defining $\Theta_A,\Theta_C$, are isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph 4: actual coefficient categories, invertibility and normalization

proof.text:
At level $n$, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] compares finite and ambient adjuncts for $A_T\to(P_n)_T$. On the diagram sites use the two factorizations of the same ringed morphism through $(\mathcal T_U,\Delta A_U)$ and $(\mathcal T_V,Q_V)$. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $r_VRu_{*,Q}\simeq Ru_{*,\Delta A}r_U$, since restriction $r$ is exact by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Identified inverse image commutes with $r$ termwise: the underlying inverse-image section and its restricted action agree. The module adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] identifies the underlying adjuncts; [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] preserves this identity on fraction representatives. Hence these derived comparisons respect exchange mates. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] on the $\Delta A$ diagram sites with quotient diagram $Q$, input $\Delta K$, and ambient exchange $e$. Its two composite equality, with these coefficient adjunct comparisons, is
$$r(\operatorname{Ex}^{Q}_{K_\bullet})H=H'\mathcal R(e).$$
Here $\mathcal R(F)=\Delta F\otimes^LQ$. Both $H,H'$ and $\mathcal R(e)$ are precisely the strict realizations in [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization]. Cancel $H$ to obtain $r(\operatorname{Ex}^{Q}_{K_\bullet})=H'\mathcal R(e)H^{-1}=v'_\bullet$. This proves equality in the actual ambient derived strict-tower category without inferring it from constant-coefficient restrictions or evaluated arrows.

source.place: Paragraph 4: coefficient and adjunct normalizations on the diagram sites

proof.text:
Prove the finite bottom-edge equation directly in the quotient-coefficient category. Abbreviate $G=Lg_n^*$, $G'=Lg_n'^*$, $R=Rf_{*,n}$, $J=Rf'_{*,n}$, $x=v'_n$, and $\Phi=\Phi_{Y'}$. The two pastings of pullback squares around the specified Frobenius cube agree, because its commutation identifications are coherent. Taking their mates using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], including its change-of-adjunction clause, and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker], gives the typed identity
$$x_{\Phi_XK_n}G(\beta_{f,K_n})\kappa_{g,RK_n}
=J(\kappa_{g',K_n})\beta_{f',G'K_n}\Phi(x_{K_n}).$$
Both sides map $\Phi GRK_n$ to $JG'\Phi_XK_n$. Postcompose with $JG'(\vartheta_n)$. Naturality $x_{K_n}GR(\vartheta_n)=JG'(\vartheta_n)x_{\Phi_XK_n}$, from the ambient natural transformation [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], and the defining formulas of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures] then give
$$v'_n\Theta_{B,n}=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi(v'_n).$$
This applies the generic mate identities to the actual ringed cube; it does not apply the constant-coefficient finite-Weil-rectangle node to these arrows.

The mate calculation of step 10 also takes place on the small ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Apply it there with $\vartheta_\bullet$, the coherent isomorphism in [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures]. Restrict the resulting equation to $\Delta A$. Step 9, which rests on the strict realization of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization], identifies its restricted exchange with the specified $v'_\bullet$, so the restricted equation gives $v'_\bullet\Theta_{B,\bullet}=\Theta_{D,\bullet}\Phi(v'_\bullet)$ as an equality of derived strict-tower morphisms. The two transport definitions give $H\Theta_{A,\bullet}=\Theta_{B,\bullet}\Phi(H)$ and $H'\Theta_{C,\bullet}=\Theta_{D,\bullet}\Phi(H')$. In particular $w=v'_\bullet H$ satisfies $w\Theta_{A,\bullet}=\Theta_{D,\bullet}\Phi(w)$. Evaluation gives all consecutive transition equations for the defined structures, since these are actual morphisms on the quotient diagram. No lift is inferred merely from a commuting family of evaluated derived arrows.

source.place: Paragraph 4: strict tower equation, before taking limits

proof.text:
The inverse automorphism induces the inverse equivalence on ringed module sheaves: the formulas of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and the coefficient composition identities of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identify $(F_{Y'}^{-1})_*$ with $F_{Y'}^*$. Both inverse composites are the identity, and this is an exact equivalence, also termwise on towers. Therefore [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] supplies the canonical natural isomorphism $j_Z$ used in [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures], with its stated projection identity. In particular
$$\operatorname{pr}_{Z,n}\Theta_{Z,\infty}=\Theta_{Z,n}\Phi(\operatorname{pr}_{Z,n}).$$
Here the derived limit is the total derived functor on $\operatorname{Tow}_{A_{Y'}}$. Its functoriality [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and naturality of $j$ take the strict equation for $w$ to
$$W\Theta_{A,\infty}=\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi(W),\qquad W=R\lim(w)=V'H.$$
Every limit structure is invertible, since $j$ and the strict structures are invertible. With the definitions of $\Theta_S,\Theta_T$ and the ordered identity $\xi=d^{-1}Ws_A$ from step 2, cancellation gives
$$\xi\Theta_S=d^{-1}W\Theta_{A,\infty}\Phi(s_A)=\Theta_T\Phi(\xi).$$
This uses neither chosen constant-coefficient triangles nor a uniqueness assertion for triangulated cone fillers.

source.place: Paragraph 4: canonical strict-limit structures and completed exchange

proof.text:
We check the two actual reduction edges by adjunction. For a map $p:L\to Z_n$, with $Z_n$ a $P_n$-object, its scalar-extension adjunct is $\widetilde p=\varepsilon_{Z_n}(p\otimes1)$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. If $p\Theta_L=\Theta_{Z,n}\Phi(p)$, then naturality of the counit and the pullback/tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] give
$$\widetilde p(\Theta_L\otimes1)=\varepsilon((p\Theta_L)\otimes1)
=\varepsilon(\Theta_{Z,n}\otimes1)(\Phi(p)\otimes1)
=\Theta_{Z,n}\Phi(\widetilde p).$$
The coefficient comparison is the one from [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures], so all adjuncts retain their $P_n$-linear actions. For $p=\operatorname{pr}_{A,n}s_A$, the limit projection equation and the transport definition imply the premise; its adjunct is $\sigma_n$ by step 2. Since $\alpha_n=h_n\sigma_n$ and $h_n\Theta_{A,n}=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi(h_n)$ by the transport definition, this proves
$$\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi(\alpha_n).$$

source.place: Paragraph 4: adjunct calculation and left reduction edge

proof.text:
For the right edge use $p=\operatorname{pr}_{D,n}d$. The projection equation from step 12 and $d\Theta_T=\Theta_{D,\infty}\Phi(d)$ give its equivariance premise. Its adjunct is exactly $\delta_n$: naturality of the canonical Roos projections [prop-weil-pbc-roos-triangle] gives $\operatorname{pr}_{D,n}H'=h'_n\operatorname{pr}_{C,n}$; step 3 gives $d=H'c^{-1}$. Thus taking adjuncts yields $h'_nq_{C,n}(c^{-1}\otimes1)=h'_n\tau_n=\delta_n$, using step 2. The calculation in step 13 therefore gives
$$\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi(\delta_n).$$
Tensor the completed equation of step 12 with $P_n$, using the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; it makes $\overline\xi_n$ a Weil morphism. Step 10 makes $v'_n$ a Weil morphism. Together with the two proved vertical equations and step 4, this is precisely the claimed square of Weil objects. The transition equations of step 6 respect these structures: on $B,D$ the structures are evaluations of the coherent tower morphisms of [def-weil-pbc-quotient-corner-frobenius-structures], and on the top vertices tensor naturality for the fixed $\Theta_S,\Theta_T$ applies. For identity Frobenius all these equations specialize to ordinary operator equations; for other Frobenius their source remains $\Phi$ of the relevant vertex.

source.place: Paragraph 4: right edge and the square of Weil objects

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For every $n$, the diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
S\otimes^LP_n @>{\overline\xi_n}>> T\otimes^LP_n\\
@V{\alpha_n}V{\sim}V @VV{\delta_n}V{\sim}\\
B_n @>{v'_n}>> D_n
\end{CD}
$$

commutes. Hence reduction of
$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ modulo $I^n$, conjugated
by the displayed canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly the S8
transported finite-level exchange map $v'_n=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}$.
The squares for $n+1\to n$ commute, and the assertion is natural for
compatible tower endomorphisms. Under a Frobenius-equivariant datum, use
$\Phi_{Y'}P_n=P_n$ to give the two reductions their induced Weil structures.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\alpha_n),\\
\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\delta_n),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the displayed reduction square is a square of Weil objects.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
Under $S=A_\infty$ and the direct-image completion identification
$T\simeq C_\infty$, the completed exchange map is both limit composites

$$
V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty,
$$

followed by the inverse of direct-image/limit commutation. More explicitly,
if $d:T\to D_\infty$ is direct-image/limit commutation and
$c:C_\infty\to T$ is direct-image completion, then its construction gives
$dc=H'$. Functorial finite
reduction and the component equations of the limit rectangle give

$$
\tau_n\overline\xi_n=v_n\sigma_n.
$$

Consequently the two composites around the completed reduction square are

$$
\delta_n\overline\xi_n
=h'_n\tau_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n
$$

and

$$
v'_n\alpha_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n.
$$

They are equal term by term because $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$ in the finite-level
rectangle. Naturality of finite reduction makes $\sigma_n$ and $\tau_n$
commute with $n+1\to n$, and functoriality of tensor reduction does the same
for $\overline\xi_n$. Together with the four transition equations, this
shows that the completed squares commute with $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ on every
corner. The limit construction and all four reduction edges are
operator-equivariant, so the conjugated equality is operator-natural as well.

For Frobenius, the definition of $\Theta_S$ transports
$\Theta_{A,\infty}$ across $s$, and the $n$th product-cone component followed

definition of $\Theta_T$ transports $\Theta_{D,\infty}$ across $t$, and its

blueprint_update.statement:
For every $n$, the diagram

$$
\begin{CD}
S\otimes^LP_n @>{\overline\xi_n}>> T\otimes^LP_n\\
@V{\alpha_n}V{\sim}V @VV{\delta_n}V{\sim}\\
B_n @>{v'_n}>> D_n
\end{CD}
$$

commutes. Hence reduction of
$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{comp}}_{\square,K}$ of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] modulo $I^n$, conjugated
by the displayed canonical reduction isomorphisms, is exactly the S8
transported finite-level exchange map $v'_n=\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,K_n}$.
The squares for $n+1\to n$ commute, and the assertion is natural for
compatible tower endomorphisms. Under a Frobenius-equivariant datum, use
$\Phi_{Y'}P_n=P_n$ to give the two reductions their induced Weil structures.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_n(\Theta_S\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{B,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\alpha_n),\\
\delta_n(\Theta_T\otimes1)
&=\Theta_{D,n}\Phi_{Y'}(\delta_n),
\end{aligned}
$$

and the displayed reduction square is a square of Weil objects.

proof.text:
Under $S=A_\infty$ and the direct-image completion identification
$T\simeq C_\infty$, the completed exchange map is both limit composites

$$
V'H=H'V:A_\infty\longrightarrow D_\infty,
$$

followed by the inverse of direct-image/limit commutation. More explicitly,
if $d:T\to D_\infty$ is direct-image/limit commutation and
$c:C_\infty\to T$ is direct-image completion, then its construction gives
$dc=H'$. Functorial finite
reduction and the component equations of the limit rectangle give

$$
\tau_n\overline\xi_n=v_n\sigma_n.
$$

Consequently the two composites around the completed reduction square are

$$
\delta_n\overline\xi_n
=h'_n\tau_n\overline\xi_n=h'_nv_n\sigma_n
$$

and

$$
v'_n\alpha_n=v'_nh_n\sigma_n.
$$

They are equal term by term because $h'_nv_n=v'_nh_n$ in the finite-level
rectangle. Naturality of finite reduction makes $\sigma_n$ and $\tau_n$
commute with $n+1\to n$, and functoriality of tensor reduction does the same
for $\overline\xi_n$. Together with the four transition equations, this
shows that the completed squares commute with $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ on every
corner. The limit construction and all four reduction edges are
operator-equivariant, so the conjugated equality is operator-natural as well.

For Frobenius, the definition of $\Theta_S$ transports
$\Theta_{A,\infty}$ across $s$, and the $n$th product-cone component followed
by $h_n$ is $\alpha_n$. This gives the first displayed Weil equation. The
definition of $\Theta_T$ transports $\Theta_{D,\infty}$ across $t$, and its
$n$th component is $\delta_n$, giving the second. The completed Frobenius
equation for $\overline\xi_n$, together with finite-level equivariance of
$v'_n$, now says that every arrow of the reduction square is a Weil morphism.

Tensoring the defining composite of
[def-weil-pbc-completed-base-change-map] with $P_n$ and using the
finite-reduction identifications of the reconstruction lemma and of the
completed-pullback reduction collapses it to the $n$-th component of the
rectangle equality of [lem-weil-pbc-rectangle-derived-limit], which is the
finite-level exchange isomorphism; the compatibilities with the transitions
follow from the tower structures.
